items.title: In a First for the Union, Peel Police Association Lines Up Behind Alvin Tedjo for Mayor
items.summary: According to the Peel Regional Police Association, Monday's press conference marked the union's first ever endorsement of a candidate in a Mississauga mayoral race, and it went to Ward 2 councillor Alvin Tedjo. Tedjo has represented Ward 2 since 2022 and finished second in the 2024 mayoral election behind incumbent Carolyn Parrish, who is running again this time around. The PRPA represents more than 3,800 uniformed and civilian Peel police employees. PRPA President Adrian Woolley said public safety cannot be reactive and that leadership requires having difficult conversations before problems turn into headlines. Before entering municipal politics, Tedjo worked as a communications strategist for Toronto Metropolitan University and Sheridan College. The race is shaping up to be crowded and competitive, with Tedjo facing off against Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and former Ward 7 councillor Dipika Damerla. Parrish won a byelection after Crombie left the mayor's chair to lead the Ontario Liberals, then returned to municipal politics this year after stepping down as party leader in January following the 2025 provincial election.

items.title: Yom Kippur Prompts Extra Peel Police Patrols at Mississauga, Brampton Synagogues After Belleville Shooting
items.summary: Peel police say they have stepped up patrols around places of worship and cultural centres in Mississauga and Brampton after a shooting outside a synagogue in Belleville on Sunday night. According to police in Belleville, an officer came across an individual near Bleecker Avenue and Victoria Avenue, a mostly residential part of the city located about 180 kilometres east of Toronto, and an altercation left both the officer and the individual injured and taken to hospital. The incident happened near the Sons of Jacob Synagogue during a gathering to mark Yom Kippur. Ontario's Special Investigations Unit, which is automatically called in whenever a police interaction with the public results in serious injury, has been notified and is now involved. Belleville police say they are not providing further comment while that investigation proceeds. Peel police added that through the High Holidays period, including Yom Kippur, they have increased their presence around synagogues and cultural centres across Mississauga and Brampton as a precaution.

items.title: Rescue Effort at Burning Mississauga Apartment Leaves Officer and Firefighter Injured
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say an officer and a firefighter were both hurt early Monday morning while helping residents escape a fire at an apartment building near Inverhouse Drive and Lakeshore Road West. According to police, crews responded to the blaze, which broke out in a hallway, and found several people trapped inside suffering from smoke inhalation. Acting Sgt. Amanda Steenson told reporters that one of the officers was hurt while helping a firefighter pull a resident from the building during the rescue. Ten people were taken to hospital by ambulance as a result of the fire. The cause has not yet been determined, and police say an investigation into what sparked the blaze is underway. Steenson said investigators could release suspect information later if the fire is found to have been deliberately set.

items.title: City Marks Rail Safety Week With Reminder That Crossing Tracks Illegally Can Be Deadly
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says it is using Rail Safety Week, which runs from September 21 to 27, 2026, to remind residents that walking on train tracks is illegal and dangerous, and that everyone should use designated railway crossings instead. According to the city, trains can travel at speeds up to 140 kilometres per hour and may need as much as two kilometres to come to a complete stop, meaning an approaching train is often closer and faster than it appears. The city says drivers and pedestrians should always obey the lights, bells and gates at a crossing, and should stop behind the gate or marked line and wait for a train to fully pass if signals are flashing. If lights begin flashing only after someone has already started crossing, the city says it is safer to keep going rather than stop partway across the tracks. School buses are required to stop at least five metres from the nearest rail at every crossing, even when gates are open and signals are not flashing, and bus drivers must open the door to look and listen for trains before proceeding. The city is asking drivers following a school bus to be ready to slow down at these stops.

items.title: Eleven Taken to Hospital as Investigators Call Mississauga Apartment Fire Suspicious
items.summary: CTV News reports that eleven people, including a Peel police officer, were taken to hospital after a fire broke out at a Mississauga apartment building early Monday morning. Police said most of those hurt suffered smoke inhalation, while two people sustained serious but non-life-threatening injuries. The injured officer's condition was described by paramedics as unrelated to the fire itself. Crews have since extinguished the flames, and some residents have already been allowed back into their units. Investigators have not released a cause, but police say the fire is being treated as suspicious while the scene remains secured. In an email to CP24, police said the scene will stay secured until fire investigators complete their determination.

items.title: City Outlines the First Steps Renters Should Take When Heating or Pest Problems Hit
items.summary: The City of Mississauga says renters who run into heating problems, water leaks or pest infestations as temperatures drop this fall should know what steps to take and where to find help before small issues become bigger ones. According to the city, tenants renting an apartment, basement unit, room or house can often resolve concerns faster when they act early and understand their own responsibilities alongside their landlord's. The city says heating problems in particular tend to become more noticeable, and more serious, once winter weather sets in if they are not addressed. For a maintenance or property standards concern, the city recommends contacting the landlord or property manager first, since many issues get resolved once tenants and landlords communicate directly. The city adds that renters do not need to involve the city for every housing problem, and that doing so is best reserved for situations that cannot be worked out with a landlord alone. Officials say fall is a good time for renters to learn what help is available before colder weather makes problems harder to manage.

items.title: Council Hits Pause on Big Data Centres While Mississauga Rewrites the Rulebook
items.summary: Mississauga city council approved an interim control bylaw on September 16 that puts a temporary hold on new applications for large-scale data centre development while staff review the city's planning policies for the sector, according to Ontario Construction News. The bylaw blocks new major digital infrastructure projects with a total peak power demand of 10 megawatts or more, and it applies citywide to conversions and expansions of existing facilities as well as brand new ones, for up to a year. An interim control bylaw lets a municipality temporarily prohibit a type of development while it studies the right long-term planning approach, and city staff will now examine whether Mississauga's Official Plan and Zoning By-law need to change. The review will also weigh new guidance from the Ontario government's Data Centre Playbook. The city says residents will have chances to weigh in during the review, and an interim report laying out its scope and timeline is expected to go to council later this year. Once the study wraps up, staff plan to bring council recommendations on how the city should regulate data centres and similar large digital infrastructure projects going forward.

items.title: Peel Police Link Suspect to 71-Vehicle Break-In Spree Across Mississauga
items.summary: Peel Regional Police say they are searching for a woman connected to a spree of vehicle break-ins that hit neighbourhoods across Mississauga during the early morning hours of September 3 and September 6. According to investigators, the vehicles were entered by smashing windows or through doors that had been left unlocked, and valuables were taken from inside. Police say 71 vehicles in total were targeted, none were stolen, and all were unoccupied when the break-ins happened. Andrea Cederberg, 33, of no fixed address, is wanted on 23 counts of attempting to commit an indictable offence, nine counts each of mischief over $5,000 and theft under $5,000, and one count of theft over $5,000. Police say the investigation is connected to the earlier arrest of Cory Lowden, 34, also of no fixed address. Investigators say they have identified possible links to similar vehicle-related crimes being investigated in Halton Region, Toronto, York Region and Waterloo Region, and are working with other Greater Toronto Area police services to determine the full scope of the alleged activity.

items.title: Peel's Vaccine Record Crackdown Led to Nearly 9,000 Student Suspensions Last Year
items.summary: Peel Public Health confirms that 8,875 students across Mississauga, Brampton and Caledon were suspended during the region's 2025-26 immunization enforcement cycle over incomplete vaccination records, following warnings issued last year that suspensions were coming. The region says the threat was not an empty one, and it is now flagging that roughly 27,500 students will have their immunization records reviewed again during the 2026-27 school year. According to Peel Public Health, students with incomplete records could once again face suspension unless their information is updated or a valid exemption is provided. The new total follows an earlier warning that 15,861 students were potentially facing suspension during the prior school year, a figure tied to students whose records did not meet provincial requirements at the time. Peel says that March figure was only a snapshot that shifted week to week as families submitted updated vaccination information. The final count of 8,875 suspensions shows that Peel Public Health does follow through on enforcing the suspension provision when families do not comply.

items.title: Streetsville, Port Credit and Meadowvale Each Hosted a Terry Fox Run This Past Sunday
items.summary: Mississauga hosted three Terry Fox Run events on Sunday, September 20, in Streetsville, Port Credit and Meadowvale, part of the annual national effort to raise money in Terry Fox's memory, according to a city press release. Registration for the non-competitive, all-inclusive runs remained open leading into the weekend for individuals, teams, or anyone who wanted to join an existing team. Organizers say proceeds collected through the three Mississauga locations go toward cancer research, consistent with how the Terry Fox Run has operated nationally since it began. The Streetsville, Port Credit and Meadowvale routes each had their own registration window and starting point, giving residents a choice of which neighbourhood run best fit their Sunday plans. The event has become a fixture of the Mississauga fall calendar, with past runs in the region drawing steady community turnout. Online sign-up remained the easiest way for participants to register ahead of race day.
